stem: The table shows Plains states growing from 300,000 to 5 million people while Native land fell by two-thirds. What is the best conclusion to draw from those two facts together?

stimulus.source_note: Figures from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 8; 5 Steps to a 5, 2024, Chapter 17; and the Unit 6 period review (land-loss figures).
stimulus.text:
| Measure | Figure |
| Native land held by tribes, 1887 | about 138 million acres |
| Native land held by tribes, 1934 | about 48 million acres |
| Population of Minnesota, the Dakotas, Kansas, and Nebraska, 1865 | about 300,000 |
| Population of the same states, 1900 | about 5 million |
| Homestead claims proved up by 1900 | 610,000 claims, 85 million acres |
| Homesteaders who had given up their farms by 1900 | about two-thirds |

options.text: The population growth caused the Dawes Act to be repealed
options.misconception: Background: the Dawes Act stayed in force until 1934; population growth did not repeal it.

options.text: Native peoples moved east and became the new Plains farmers
options.misconception: Background: Native peoples were confined to reservations and lost land; they did not become the new Plains farmers.

options.text: Settlement and Native land loss were two sides of one expansion
The Homestead Act gave land only to Native peoples
options.misconception: Background: the Homestead Act gave land to settlers; Native peoples lost land under allotment.

rationales.A: Background: the Dawes Act stayed in force until 1934. Population growth did not repeal it.
rationales.B: Background: Native peoples were confined to reservations and lost land. They did not become the new Plains farmers.
rationales.C: The same decades that filled the Plains with five million settlers stripped the tribes of 90 million acres. Background: the land the settlers farmed was, in large part, land taken from Native peoples through allotment and the sale of 'surplus' land.
rationales.D: Background: the Homestead Act gave land to settlers. Native peoples lost land under allotment.
rationales.general:
Picture two lines on one graph: settlers rising, tribal land falling, in the same years.
1. Read the first line. Plains states grow from 300,000 people to 5 million.
2. Read the second line. Tribal land falls from 138 million acres to 48 million.
3. Name the link. One expansion, two results: settlers gained the land the tribes lost.
Remember: when two lines move together, ask whether one line is feeding on the other.
